Problem: Patients phone the GP practice for routine questions and appointments, which ties up reception staff and creates long phone queues.
Measures:
- 60% of routine questions answered without a phone call
- Every answer cites an approved source
- 100% of red-flag symptoms sent to 999 or NHS 111
- Hallucination rate under 2% on the evaluation set
- No personal data in logs
In scope:
- Practice FAQs (opening hours, repeat prescriptions, registration)
- Booking, moving and cancelling appointments
- Sending urgent cases to 999 or NHS 111
- Masking personal data before logging
Out of scope:
- Diagnosis or symptom advice
- Medication or dose advice
- Reading or changing medical records
- Payments

Problem: GPs spend a large part of each day writing up consultation notes, which cuts the time available for patients.
Measures:
- Admin time per consultation down by 30%
- 100% of summaries approved by a clinician before saving
- Every summary line linked to its source note
- No facts added that are not in the notes (faithfulness check)
- Every action audited
In scope:
- Structured summaries of consultation notes
- Flagging missing or unclear information
- Clinician review, edit and approval
- Audit trail of every action
Out of scope:
- Saving without clinician approval
- Clinical decisions or treatment advice
- Coding (SNOMED or ICD)
- Writing directly to the clinical system

Problem: Referral letters take GPs a long time to write and patients often do not understand what their referral means.
Measures:
- Time to produce a referral letter down by 50%
- 100% of letters signed off by a clinician before sending
- Patient copy at reading age 11 or below
- Exports meet WCAG 2.2 AA
In scope:
- Drafting referral letters from the approved summary and practice template
- Clinician review and sign-off
- Plain-language patient copy
- Accessible PDF and HTML export
Out of scope:
- Sending letters without sign-off
- Choosing the specialist or service
- Booking hospital appointments
- Using data not in the approved summary
